open_points.subject: A21 security review boundary coverage
open_points.text: State 0 adds: “An agent's own access to a service … is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel”; A21 says its review “covers every actor and boundary accepted in State 0” but lists only “the microservices the kernel calls over their HTTP APIs,” not the new direct agent-to-service boundary.
open_points.question: Must the direct agent-to-microservice channel receive an outcome in the State 2 security review, or is A21's completeness claim limited to boundaries controlled by the kernel?
options: Include the direct channel in A21 and assess its applicable security categories
Declare the direct channel outside A21 and narrow A21's completeness claim
Treat the existing microservices entry as covering both kernel and direct-agent access
open_points.default_guess: Declare the direct channel outside the kernel's security review and narrow A21's completeness claim accordingly.

open_points.subject: personal-data disclosure boundary
open_points.text: The changed exclusion says “its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns,” while the actor text says “the owner alone reads them” and A07 concludes “no agent ever holds it.” The same change permits an agent to access a service directly and process a photo outside the kernel.
open_points.question: May a service give an agent personal data through the direct channel, or does the owner-only-reader rule prohibit that channel from carrying personal data despite being outside kernel control?
options: K-14 and A07 govern only kernel disclosures; the service may separately authorize direct personal-data access
The owner-only-reader rule is global, so direct agent access must never expose personal data
Direct service data must first be assigned a kernel disclosure class, after which K-14 applies
open_points.default_guess: Treat K-14 and A07 as constraints only on kernel disclosures and leave direct access to the service and owner.

open_points.subject: MCP listener isolation
open_points.text: State 0 now says the reverse proxy “is the only client of the kernel's listener” and the host “does not expose [it] otherwise,” while M28 and A17 merely configure an unrestricted `mcp_listen_address` and name no check establishing either condition.
open_points.question: Is proxy-only reachability an unchecked deployment assumption, or must the kernel restrict or verify the configured listener address before starting?
options: Make it an explicit host deployment assumption that the kernel does not verify
Restrict the listener to a locally enforceable address or socket form
Require a startup check that verifies proxy-only reachability
open_points.default_guess: Treat proxy-only reachability as an operational host assumption and let the kernel bind the configured address without verifying network exposure.
